blocks.x: Fall in the Adirondacks is hard to beat, but there’s one Upstate New York lake that has even more reason to be on your autumn radar this year.

Lake George was named the runner-up for Best Lake in USA Today’s 2026 10Best Readers’ Choice Awards, adding a major national accolade to a destination that has been drawing visitors to its shores for more than a century. And come October, its mountain-lined waters become an especially spectacular backdrop for fall foliage.

Known as the “Queen of American Lakes,” the cozy destination sits along the southern edge of the Adirondacks, surrounded by mountains and forests that burst into shades of red, orange, and gold each fall. The lake itself stretches for roughly 32 miles, meaning there are plenty of ways to take in the scenery—from waterfront viewpoints and mountain hikes to getting out on the water.
Here’s everything to know about visiting Lake George for fall foliage season.

Source / William Mahar, Getty Images
Why Lake George Voted So Highly in USA TODAY’s 10Best
Lake George balances historic charm with outdoor adventure better than almost anywhere else in the Northeast.

32 Miles of Unbroken Scenery: Flanked by peak after peak, the shorelines are protected from heavy industrial development, preserving natural mountain slopes that drop straight into crystal-clear waters.
A Century of Heritage: From 19th-century Gilded Age estates along “Millionaires’ Row” to historic steamships, the area offers rich history alongside world-class views.
Multi-Element Adventure: You can hike a mountain summit in the morning, take a boat tour or paddle in the afternoon, and dine right on the water at night.
Prime Foliage Timing: When to See Peak Autumn Colors
While timing shifts slightly each year based on weather and elevation, the foliage window in the southern Adirondacks follows a reliable timeline:
Late September (Early Color): Hints of yellow and light orange appear along higher ridges and northern bays.

Early to Mid-October (Peak Colors): This is the sweet spot. Leaves reach 80% to 100% transformation, painting the shoreline in deep crimsons, burnt oranges, and golds. Columbus Day / Indigenous Peoples’ Day weekend is historically the busiest and most vibrant period.
Late October (Late/Past Peak): Golden and amber leaves drop, opening up expansive views through the forest tree line.

Source / Lake George Chamber of Comerce
Can’t-Miss Sites & Autumn Experiences
Explore Bolton Landing — Cruise along Route 9N’s western shoreline for lake lookouts, craft shops, apple orchards, and a classic Upstate New York road-trip experience.
Drive up Prospect Mountain — Take the 5.5-mile Veterans Memorial Highway to sweeping views of Lake George and the Adirondacks, with vistas stretching up to 100 miles on clear days.
Cruise Lake George — See the fall foliage from the water aboard historic vessels like The Mohican or the steam-powered Minne-Ha-Ha.
Hike to panoramic lookouts — Choose from scenic trails like The Pinnacle, Buck Mountain, or Shelving Rock for mountain and lake views.

Source / Lake George
Top Waterfront Dining & Drink Spots
The Boathouse Restaurant (Lake George / Cresthaven): Upscale-casual dining set inside an authentic boathouse with deck seating right on the water. Known for steaks, fresh seafood, and lobster rolls.
The Algonquin Restaurant (Bolton Landing): An iconic dock-and-dine favorite featuring classic Adirondack lodge aesthetics, seafood scampi, and sweeping bay views.
Tavern on the Lake at Blue Water Manor (Bolton Landing): Lively, laid-back deck dining elevated high above the water with great craft cocktails and panoramic mountain vistas.
Lake George Beach Club (Lake George Village): Two stories of covered outdoor decks right next to Shepard Park Beach, ideal for pub fare, drinks, and live music.
The Lakehouse at The Sagamore Resort (Bolton Landing): Open-air dining set on a luxury island resort enclave, delivering high-end cocktails and scenic views across the lake.
